claims.text: Elevated-temperature cyclic or sustained near-yield loading promotes stress-assisted diffusion in an initially single-phase HEA.
Stress-assisted diffusion produces local compositional fluctuations and short-range ordering.
Stress-induced ordering nucleates nanoscale ordered intermetallic-like phases.
The ordered regions preferentially form at grain boundaries, dislocation channels, or slip bands because these are high-stress regions.
B2 is an ordered phase that can occur in a high-entropy alloy.
B2 or similar ordered nanoclusters are brittle embrittling sites.
Localized ordered nanoclusters impair the alloy's overall toughness even when their spatial extent is limited.
Relative to an unloaded same-temperature or lower-temperature baseline, the loaded sample will have reduced toughness or fracture strain.
The toughness reduction will be accompanied by newly formed nanoscale ordered regions detectable by TEM, APT, or high-resolution diffraction.
The proposed mechanism can operate below temperatures that cause conventional grain coarsening or complete bulk phase separation.
At very low temperature or very low stress, the alloy retains its initial toughness because diffusion-assisted ordering is inactive.
The initial baseline is a uniform single-phase FCC or BCC solid solution without pre-existing brittle intergranular precipitates.
The baseline single-phase HEA has high toughness.
The length scale or size distribution of ordered decomposition can vary with alloy composition and thermal treatment.
The critical stress and temperature thresholds for stress-assisted ordering vary with alloy composition and processing history.
